title: Feature: RangeInput
body:
**Summary**

Fix #2317 

* Finally choose to implement `RangeInput` with the connector `connectRangeSlider` instead of `connectPriceRanges` because the logic was really the same. Maybe try in upcoming versions to manage `PriceRanges` with `connectRange` both share similarities (boundaries, range).

* The markup is the same as RIS

* Deprecation for the connector `connectRangeSlider` for `connectRange`

* Jest enzyme serializer added to be able to handle Snapshots with Enzyme

**Result**

You can play with the `RangeInput` on dev-novel.

comments.body:
Deploy preview ready!

Built with commit 26f2e6dec8475672c5f9ceeb1fa8ec9cd08f6b7c

https://deploy-preview-2440--algolia-instantsearch.netlify.com

Due to the changes, now we can pass string values to the `refine` function. This allow the user to implement a range widget without caring about parsing the numbers from the rendering.

But since the signature of the `refine` function is `(Array<number,number>) => void` we should probably only handle numbers and empty values (the later is used to be able to reset the range).

WDYT?

> Due to the changes, now we can pass string values to the refine function. This allow the user to implement a range widget without caring about parsing the numbers from the rendering.

That's nice and it makes in terms of usage. What is preventing us from supporting both numbers, null and strings? I'm not sure it's consistent with other refine API's that takes numbers as parameters 🤔 but that would be a win in terms of usability.

Nothing prevent us to dot it. The other connectors (that I looked) don't do validation on user input, they pass the results to the helper. But in the `connectRange` case we need to do some validations on it to be able to check the given value on boundaries.

IMO we should not trust the user inputs. We should probably do some validation in the connector to avoid to throw an error in the helper if the value is not supported (see [`valToNumber`](https://github.com/algolia/algoliasearch-helper-js/blob/7275a756510f5d7df460ae99cb88af6c2e617424/src/functions/valToNumber.js)).

After discussion (see #2464), we keep the validation on inputs for a smoother user experience. The main differences from the original implementation is that now **both** inputs **must** be valid to be able to trigger the refinement.
